lessons.man: stream editor for filtering and transforming text
lessons.what: Finds and replaces text, or deletes lines, without opening an editor.
lessons.when: Changing 'colour' to 'color' in a 300-line file in one shot.
lessons.tip: -i edits the file itself. Try without -i first!

lessons.man: pattern scanning and processing language
lessons.what: Works with text column by column, with conditions and maths.
lessons.when: Who scored above 90? What's the class total? awk does it in one line.
lessons.tip: $1 = 1st column. -F, for CSV files.

lessons.man: build and execute command lines from standard input
lessons.what: Turns a list from one command into arguments for another.
lessons.when: find gave you 40 .tmp files. Delete them all in one go.
lessons.tip: -print0 + -0 handles file names with spaces safely.

lessons.man: format and print data
lessons.what: Prints text with exact formatting: padding, decimals, alignment.
lessons.when: Making neat tables or rounded numbers in your scripts.
lessons.tip: Unlike echo, printf doesn't add a newline. Use \n.

lessons.man: print a sequence of numbers
lessons.what: Prints a list of numbers.
lessons.when: Creating folders lab1 to lab10 without typing ten commands.
example: $ for i in $(seq 1 10); do mkdir lab$i; done
lessons.tip: seq 0 5 20 counts in steps of 5.

quiz.why: Without g, only the first match per line changes.
Names are separated by a null byte, not spaces.

lessons.man: execute a program periodically, showing output fullscreen
lessons.what: Re-runs a command every few seconds and shows the live result.
lessons.when: Watching a download folder grow, or disk space drop, live.
lessons.tip: -d highlights what changed. Ctrl + C to exit.

lessons.man: Report time consumed by pipeline's execution.
lessons.what: Measures how long a command takes to run.
lessons.when: Your code is 'slow'. How slow? Measure before you fix.
lessons.tip: 'real' is the actual clock time you waited.

lessons.man: run a command with a time limit
lessons.what: Stops a command automatically if it runs too long.
lessons.when: Testing code that might get stuck in an infinite loop.
lessons.tip: Exit code 124 means 'timed out'.

lessons.man: run a program with modified scheduling priority
lessons.what: Starts a program with lower (or higher) CPU priority.
lessons.when: Running a heavy task but you still want your laptop to feel smooth.
lessons.tip: -20 = highest priority, 19 = lowest. Higher = nicer.

lessons.man: alter priority of running processes
lessons.what: Changes the priority of a program that's already running.
lessons.when: Forgot to use nice and the task is hogging your CPU.
lessons.tip: Raising priority (negative values) needs sudo.

quiz.q: Which nice value is the LOWEST priority?

quiz.why: It changes a running process's priority.

lessons.man: print system information
lessons.what: Shows your kernel name, version and machine type.
lessons.when: A tutorial says 'needs kernel 6+'. Which one do you have?
lessons.tip: -a shows everything at once.

lessons.man: display information about the CPU architecture
lessons.what: Shows details about your processor.
lessons.when: How many cores do you have for that parallel programming lab?
lessons.tip: nproc gives just the core count.

lessons.man: print or control the kernel ring buffer
lessons.what: Shows messages from the Linux kernel (hardware events).
lessons.when: You plugged in a USB and nothing happened. What did the kernel see?
lessons.tip: -w watches new messages live.

lessons.man: Control the systemd system and service manager
lessons.what: Starts, stops and checks background services.
lessons.when: Bluetooth stopped working. Restart the service instead of rebooting.
lessons.tip: enable = start automatically at boot.

lessons.man: Print log entries from the systemd journal
lessons.what: Reads system logs for services.
lessons.when: A service keeps failing. The logs tell you why.
lessons.tip: -u picks a service, -f follows live.

lessons.man: maintain crontab files for individual users
lessons.what: Schedules commands to run automatically at set times.
lessons.when: Auto-backup your notes every night at 11 PM. Set it once, forget it.
example: # min hour day month weekday command
lessons.tip: */10 * * * * = every 10 minutes.

lessons.man: queue, examine, or delete jobs for later execution
lessons.what: Runs a command once, at a specific future time.
lessons.when: 'Remind me in 30 minutes' style one-time tasks.
lessons.tip: cron = repeat. at = one time only.

lessons.man: Control the system time and date
lessons.what: Shows and sets the system clock and time zone.
lessons.when: Your clock shows the wrong time after travelling.
lessons.tip: list-timezones shows every zone.

lessons.man: Control the system hostname
lessons.what: Shows or changes your computer's name and OS details.
lessons.when: Renaming 'localhost' to something cooler.
lessons.tip: Also a quick way to see your OS version.

lessons.man: enter messages into the system log
lessons.what: Writes your own message into the system log.
lessons.when: Your backup script can log 'backup done' for later checking.
lessons.tip: Great for leaving notes from your scripts.

quiz.q: Which command sets the time zone?

quiz.why: It lists the Operating System line.

lessons.man: create a new user or update default new user information
lessons.what: Creates a new user account.
lessons.when: Your sibling wants their own login on the family PC.
lessons.tip: -m creates their home folder, -s sets their shell.

lessons.man: modify a user account
lessons.what: Changes an existing user: groups, shell, name and more.
lessons.when: Giving a user access to the 'docker' group.
lessons.tip: ALWAYS use -aG. -G alone replaces all groups!

lessons.man: delete a user account and related files
lessons.what: Deletes a user account.
lessons.when: The guest account isn't needed anymore.
lessons.tip: -r also deletes their home folder. Be sure!

lessons.man: create a new group
lessons.what: Creates a new user group.
lessons.when: Making a 'project' group so teammates share one folder.
lessons.tip: Groups + chgrp + chmod = shared folders.

lessons.man: change user password expiry information
lessons.what: Sets when a user's password expires.
lessons.when: Forcing a new user to change their password on first login.
lessons.tip: -d 0 = must change password at next login.
